title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rotary/rope optimizations
author: Nikhil Rao
description:
Context: The serving runtime has long used an in-house attention kernel with heuristic optimizations. Recent work upstream (FlashAttention v2) and our internal experiments indicate substantial throughput and memory improvements when switching to the v2 kernels combined with fused rotary/rope application and fused QKV projection kernels.

This PR: Integrates FlashAttention v2 as an optional kernel path, implements fused rotary/ROPE application for the common rotary embeddings codepath, and introduces a small fused-QKV kernel for models that benefit from a single projection operation. It also includes scheduler hints to preferentially route short-sequence/low-latency traffic to the new kernels, and KV-cache layout adjustments to avoid extra copies when using the fused ops.

Key goals: improve throughput and GPU memory utilization, reduce per-token latency for production workloads, and maintain functional parity & numerical stability.

Compatibility and rollout: The new kernels are behind a runtime feature-flag (ATTN_USE_FLASHAV2) and a model-capability flag in the model registry. We validated correctness against our existing attention implementation across a wide battery of unit/float32/float16 tests. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pools, metric monitoring for perplexity/regression, automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Notes: This PR focuses on the runtime/kernel integration and scheduler changes. Additional documentation and model registry updates follow in a separate PR to keep the change surface manageable.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial vendor import of FlashAttention v2 kernels; implement fused-rope CUDA kernel and unit tests; add optional fused QKV projection; KV-cache layout adjustments and copy elimination; scheduler routing hints and config flagging; small CI fixes and benchmark harness updates.
files_changed_snippets: serving/runtime/attention/attention_kernel.h: added enum KernelBackend { DEFAULT, FLASH_V2_FUSED } and selector logic based on model flags.
serving/runtime/kv_cache/cache_layout.h: introduced contiguous-kv layout variant to support zero-copy fused ops when ATT_USE_FLASHAV2 is enabled.
serving/runtime/scheduler/batcher.cpp: added routeHint = KernelBackend::FLASH_V2_FUSED for short-seq inference traffic under perf profile 'low-latency'.
review_comments: Ava Thompson (2024-11-19): Left a few nit comments on API naming and feature-flag default. Also requested clarity on numeric stability tests for rotary embedding edge-cases.
Nikhil Rao (2024-11-19): Addressed the naming nits and added additional unit tests for boundary rotary frequencies. Explained rationale for default=false flag to avoid surprising regressions.
Jun Park (2024-11-20): Questioned KV-cache layout change impact on existing hot caches; asked for benchmark comparing cache-miss scenarios.

Nikhil Rao (2024-11-20): Added benchmark results to the PR description and a micro-benchmark (benchmarks/attention/attention_bench.py) showing 18-34% throughput improvement across GPT-like configs and 9-15% reduction in p95 latency for short sequences.
Sofia Martinez (2024-11-22): Approved after tests. Requested follow-up PR to update model registry and default rollout policy once canary is validated.
CI (2024-11-25): Reran after rebase; all CUDA tests and python integration tests passed.
release_notes:
- Added optional FlashAttention v2 kernel path with fused rotary/ROPE application and fused QKV projection.
- Introduced KV-cache layout optimization to eliminate extra copies when using fused ops.
- Scheduler hints to route low-latency traffic to the new kernels.
- Feature-flagged rollout (ATTN_USE_FLASHAV2=false by default).
